verdict: McDonald's grew revenue 5% to $6.2B and operating income 8% to $2.7B as global comparable sales rose 1.9% — a 13th straight positive quarter — though licensed markets stayed under pressure from the war in the Middle East.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago; +4% in constant currencies

segments.name: Franchised restaurants
segments.note: Rent and royalties paid by the local owners who run most McDonald's restaurants — the heart of the business model.

segments.name: Company-owned restaurants
segments.note: Food and drink sold at restaurants McDonald's runs itself.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Fees and other income beyond rent, royalties and restaurant sales.

segmentNote: Comparable sales rose in two of three segments: U.S. +2.5% on higher average checks from menu price increases, International Operated Markets +2.7% led by the U.K. and Germany, and International Developmental Licensed Markets -0.2% on the continued impact of the war in the Middle East. Systemwide sales to loyalty members were over $6B in the quarter.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Head office, marketing support and running the global franchising machine — $721M of SG&A (including $99M of depreciation and amortization), less $17M of other operating income, net.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $372M on McDonald's debt, partly offset by $45M of net nonoperating income.
footerNote: The release's rounded lines sum to $3,434M of operating costs against the $3,433M printed, and its printed $479M tax provision implies net income $1M above the reported $1,929M; the two $1M rounding differences are carried in the SG&A and tax lines so this page ties exactly to reported operating income of $2,736M and net income of $1,929M.

takeaways.title: Comparable sales stayed positive
takeaways.text: Global comparable sales rose 1.9% — a 13th consecutive positive quarter: the U.S. grew 2.5% on higher average checks, International Operated Markets 2.7% led by the U.K. and Germany, and Developmental Licensed Markets slipped 0.2% on the war in the Middle East.

takeaways.title: Revenue grew 5%
takeaways.text: Total revenue rose 5% to $6,169M (+4% in constant currencies): franchised rent and royalties rose 4% to $3,723M and company-run restaurant sales rose 6% to $2,355M.

takeaways.title: Charges trimmed EPS slightly
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 8% to $2,736M despite $35M of pre-tax restructuring charges for 'Accelerating the Organization.' Excluding charges, EPS was $2.70 versus the reported $2.66.

oneTimers: Pre-tax charges of $35M ($0.04 per share), primarily restructuring charges for 'Accelerating the Organization,' the company's internal modernization program. Excluding them, EPS was $2.70.
